title.en: Poem: The Tale of Custard the Dragon (Ogden Nash)
Boasting heroes hide, the 'coward' saves all

text.en: Belinda's house is full of boastful pets—a mouse who chases lions, a dog tough as a tiger—while poor dragon Custard begs for a safe cage. Then a real pirate climbs the window!

Ogden Nash's The Tale of Custard the Dragon is a witty ballad—a story told in playful rhyming four-line stanzas (aabb) full of fun coinages like 'realio, trulio'.
Belinda lives in a little white house with four pets: a little black kitten Ink, grey mouse Blink, yellow dog Mustard, and a dragon named Custard.
Ink, Blink, and Mustard claim tremendous courage—braver than barrels of bears or tigers in rage—while Custard has fierce spikes, fire-mouth, and dagger toes yet always cries for a 'nice safe cage', earning relentless teasing.
Everything flips when a frightening pirate with a wooden leg, cutlass, and two pistols bursts through the window. Belinda screams, Mustard flees yelping, Ink bolts downstairs, and Blink vanishes into a mousehole.
Only Custard springs forward like an engine, clashes his tail like irons in a dungeon, charges the pirate like a robin after a worm, and swallows him whole! Afterward the pets resume boasting twice as loud—while modest Custard still happily asks for his nice safe cage.

caption.en: Trace imagery, tone and central idea

text.en: The Tale of Custard the Dragon by Ogden Nash is a hilarious ballad that flips our ideas about loud boasts vs real bravery.
What is a ballad? A poem that tells an eventful story in lively rhyming stanzas, here in aabb couplets.
Belinda keeps four pets in her little white house: black kitten Ink, little mouse Blink, yellow dog Mustard, and Custard the dragon.
Nash playfully invents funny words like 'realio, trulio' using poetic licence to create cheerful rhythm.
Notice the irony in Custard's body: he has sharp teeth, fireplace mouth, chimney nose, and daggers on his toes.
Despite all that natural armour, Custard simply asks for a nice safe cage, so Belinda and the pets tickle and mock him mercilessly.
Ink and Blink boast they chase lions down the stairs, while Mustard insists he is as brave as a furious tiger.
Suddenly real danger strikes: a pirate climbs through the window with pistols in both hands, a cutlass, and a wooden leg.
Under real threat, every boaster collapses: Belinda pales and cries help, Mustard flees yelping, Ink hides down below, and Blink darts into a hole.
Up leaps 'cowardly' Custard! Nash uses three strong similes: snorting like an engine, clashing his tail like dungeon irons, charging like a robin at a worm.
The pirate fires two wild shots that miss, and Custard gobbles the pirate whole without leaving a scrap.
Once danger passes, look what the three boasters say: Mustard says he got confused, and Ink and Blink claim they would have been three times braver!
And Custard? Calm and humble, he agrees that everybody is braver than him—and still politely requests a nice safe cage.
Nash's message is timeless: true courage proves itself quietly in crisis, whereas empty boasting hides when trouble knocks.

problem.en: Analyse the three similes describing Custard's attack and explain the closing irony of the ballad.

text.en: Snorted 'like an engine': captures thunderous power and fiery steam.

why.en: Contrasts sharply with his earlier gentle tears.

text.en: Clashed tail 'like irons in a dungeon': shows metallic heaviness and frightening sound.

why.en: Shows physical force turned active only when friends need saving.

text.en: At the end, the others resume empty boasting while Custard agrees modestly.

why.en: Irony exposes how boasters take comfort back easily after someone else saves them.

prompt.en: How do Ink, Blink, and Mustard behave before, during, and after the pirate attack compared to Custard?

requiredIdeas.en: Before: Ink, Blink, and Mustard boast loudly and mock Custard's wish for a safe cage
During: All three run away and hide while Custard charges and swallows the pirate
After: Boasters make excuses and boast again while modest Custard stays humble

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Custard stayed timid during the actual pirate attack

points.en: Ogden Nash uses a comic ballad (aabb stanzas) with invented words ('realio, trulio') and vivid similes.
Ink, Blink, and Mustard brag endlessly about courage yet vanish the moment an armed pirate arrives.
'Cowardly' Custard bravely leaps up like an engine, blocks the crisis, and swallows the pirate whole.
Afterward the boasters invent excuses while Custard stays modest—proving real bravery shows in action, not talk.
